To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mitochondria isolated from rat livers during the acute stage of Fasciola hepatica infection have a reduced capacity to couple respiration with ATP production.
the liver fluke, Fasciola hepatica, induces mitochondrial dysfunction in the livers of infected rats.
mitochondrial respiratory properties and energy-linked reactions were perturbed in rats infected with the trematode Fasciola hepatica.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the parasite Fasciola on the liver of the rat.
the effects of Fasciola hepatica on mitochondrial function in the liver of rats.
the biochemical and physiological changes that occur in the mitochondria of the liver during the acute and chronic stages of Fasciola hepatica infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver fluke infection causes a profound disruption of mitochondrial function in the liver of the rat host.
the parasite induces changes in the mitochondrial respiratory system, and these changes are not fully reversible.

mitochondrial respiratory control and oligomycin-sensitive ATP synthesis were markedly perturbed at 4 weeks, and to a lesser extent at 6 weeks, after infection with Fasciola hepatica; these perturbations were still present, but to a lesser degree, at later stages of infection.
the parasite Fasciola causes a progressive and irreversible uncoupling of mitochondrial respiration, which is most severe at 4 weeks, but is still evident 21 weeks post infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver fluke, Fasciola hepatica, induces a profound uncoupling of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, which persists for at least 6 weeks after infection.
the parasite Fasciola can induce aberrant energy-linked mitochondrial reactions, which could be a potential target for future anti-fluke drugs.
F. hepatica infection causes mitochondrial dysfunction that persists for at least 6 weeks postinfection.
